comparability_risks.backbone: Paper uses GPT-5; current API model identifier is gpt-5.6-sol, a different provider-selected backbone.
comparability_risks.selection: R24 is20 selected questions,10 FinQA; prior live rounds on same selection are r21,r22,r23. This is now a reused regression set, not fresh full-test evidence.
comparability_risks.negative_weight: FinQA R24 negative share2/10=20%; paper Table4 is97/1099=8.8262%. Different mixture changes Total even at identical stratum accuracies.
comparability_risks.precision: Reference-display R24=70%; fixed2 diagnostic=40%. Paper gives no explicit rule choosing reference decimal places, so claims of exact same scoring require qualification. Do not switch precision after observing outcomes.
comparability_risks.native_display: Bare FinQA references lack unit labels; document reporting scale can refer to another column or unrelated paragraph. Amount outputs may be dollars while a neighboring table column is millions. One global document scale cannot establish all target units.
comparability_risks.main_score_policy: Keep all original samples, labels and errors in main denominator. Do not drop three conflicts, replace main labels or count source-sensible abstention as benchmark-correct.
comparability_risks.small_n: 10 questions are insufficient to establish attainment of paper full-benchmark accuracy;100% abstention is only2/2.

paper_counterfactual_count_vs_reported_a.interpretation: Reported98.80% is not attainable as an integer recall with denominator97 at two-decimal rounding. This is an unresolved paper reporting/count discrepancy, not justification to change labels or reported reference.

minimal_recommendations: Continue to report Total and unanswerable recall with explicit numerator/denominator, plus answerable accuracy and false abstentions separately.
Freeze and disclose precision policy before new validation; retain fixed2 and reference_display side by side until ambiguity is resolved.
Do not conflate a reported approximate quantity with a source-grounded exact calculation; preserve qualifiers and fee scope.
Keep benchmark scores and evidence-quality findings separate for MKTX/CDNS/AMT.
Address explicit unit-metadata erasure conservatively, with positive and incompatible-unit negative tests, without number-magnitude heuristics.
